back: A financial contract granting the buyer the right (not obligation) to BUY the underlying asset at the specified strike price on or before expiration.
A financial contract granting the buyer the right (not obligation) to SELL the underlying asset at the specified strike price on or before expiration.

front: How do rights and risk profiles differ between an Option Buyer and an Option Seller?
back: The Buyer pays a premium and holds the RIGHT to exercise (downside capped at premium). The Seller receives the premium and assumes the OBLIGATION to perform if exercised.

front: What is the rule for an In-the-Money (ITM) Call option?
back: Spot Price is greater than Strike Price (S > K). Exercising allows buying the asset below current market value.

front: What is the rule for an In-the-Money (ITM) Put option?
back: Spot Price is less than Strike Price (S < K). Exercising allows selling the asset above current market value.

front: What does At-the-Money (ATM) mean for both Calls and Puts?
back: Spot Price equals Strike Price (S = K). Neither option possesses intrinsic exercise profit.
